Ui.Script: -- Ref Cooldown.lua's CooldownFrame_SetTimer, re-expressed: show-and-arm only when all three -- are positive, else hide. -- -- THE ONE FORK, and why it is two faithful branches rather than a guard. The reference's -- body arms a Model (`this.start = start … this:SetSequence(0)`); ours arms our native -- <Cooldown> widget, which is where 0263 put that machine. -- -- **Since decision 1751 the fork is almost never taken, and that is the fix.** The loader -- now materializes a `<Model>` whose file IS the cooldown indicator as a real `<Cooldown>` -- (`loader::frame_kind_of`) — the file is the thing's identity, and this engine draws that -- sweep natively. So `<Model … inherits="CooldownFrameTemplate"/>`, which is what every -- real caller writes (the reference's own ContainerFrameItemButtonTemplate, its action -- buttons, three corpus addons), arrives here as a Cooldown and sweeps. -- -- The `if this.SetCooldown` guard stays for the case that remains: a Model built with -- some OTHER file, or a plain frame handed in by an addon. Calling SetCooldown -- unconditionally is what shipped, and it raised on exactly that: a Bagnon slot holding an -- item with a live cooldown died on `attempt to call method 'SetCooldown' (a nil value)` -- — and, because !OmniCC wraps this very function, it took OmniCC's countdown down with -- it. That branch shows and hides the frame and nothing more, which is a missing visual, -- not a broken window. function CooldownFrame_SetTimer(this, start, duration, enable) if ( start > 0 and duration > 0 and enable > 0 ) then if ( this.SetCooldown ) then this:SetCooldown(start, duration) end this:Show() else this:Hide() end end
